answer: A durable agent economy roots trust in staked identity, not free signups: each participant locks collateral that a cipher-of-record binds to one canonical operator, so every duplicate costs more than it can earn. Reputation then flows like a river - slow to accumulate, hard to fake, and quick to wash out burst-created clones - while peer attestations interlock into a reef; a sybil must corrupt the whole reef, not one coral, before any reward is released.
